ai.indexing_job: indexing_job reads better than our index_job and costs 6 points; concede if they care
ai.knowledge_group: their "searchable knowledge base" is our knowledge_collection; a vocabulary choice
ai.knowledge_item: their purpose says "document metadata" — our ai.knowledge_document
ai.suggestion_result: our ai.suggestion_outcome; their own purpose uses "result" for the value inside the row
ai.usage_policy: ours is richer, 26 columns against their 17

catalogue.membership_program: the level above the plan, which we do not have. With membership_benefit and the accepted plan_benefit this is one question: does membership become its own three-level hierarchy, or stay entitlement_template plus product?
catalogue.plan_benefit: maps benefits to a plan with usage limits

control.channel_item: matched cell_instance on noise; channel-to-item mapping
control.webhook: our control.webhook_subscription; an endpoint that selects events is a subscription

fnb.kitchen_order: our fnb.kitchen_ticket — their own purpose calls it a ticket
fnb.menu_item_modifier: join between menu_item and modifier group

fnb.order_item: their prefix removal and our word: fnb.order_line. Ours is fnb.fnb_order_line, theirs is order_item, and a line is what an order has. 0 change points — nothing references it yet

fnb.price_list: F&B/Retail stand alone; their purpose says it does not depend on Catalogue

fnb.recipe_item: their purpose says "ingredients and quantities" — our fnb.recipe_ingredient

fnb.variant: F&B/Retail stand alone; their purpose says it does not depend on Catalogue
identity.benefit_usage: use of a membership benefit against its allowance
identity.customer: a guest is marketing.guest_profile plus pii.subject; identity holds principals

identity.customer_extra_value: the value side of the pair; same placement
identity.customer_membership: the membership a customer holds; we have entitlement_template and no holder record

identity.module: a registry of authorisation modules; ours live in contracts/shared/permissions.yaml, not a table
identity.otp: ours is a 2-column stub; keep our name, take their columns
identity.permission: same — the permission vocabulary is a contract file for us, not data
identity.refresh_token: we hold session but no refresh-token rotation record
identity.user_access: assigns a role to a principal in a scope — we have role_permission and delegated_access but no grant table
identity.user_account: principal is ours and covers person, service and device, which their own purpose describes

inventory.stock_count_line: the table name repeats its schema; same habit as the 645 column renames
inventory.stock_movement: the table name repeats its schema; same habit as the 645 column renames
inventory.stock_reservation: catalogue.inventory_hold is ticket channel capacity, not physical stock, and a movement is a completed move. We cannot reserve stock for an order
inventory.stock_transfer: the table name repeats its schema; same habit as the 645 column renames
inventory.stock_transfer_line: the table name repeats its schema; same habit as the 645 column renames
inventory.supplier_contract: purchasing agreement and terms with a supplier
inventory.wastage: our inventory.movement with kind and reason. It already carries unit_cost, cost_center_id and journal_entry_id, so wastage posts to the ledger by the same path as every other movement. A separate table splits the stock ledger in two
ledger.company: our ledger.legal_entity, the accounting term and unambiguous next to control.tenant
ledger.journal: their journal is the header; ours is journal_entry with journal_line beneath it
ledger.settlement_issue: our ledger.settlement_exception; exception is the term of art for a reconciliation break
maintenance.preventive_plan: our maintenance_plan repeats the schema; theirs is more specific
maintenance.rental_damage_assessment: we give the domain its own schema; same principle they accepted for branding->whitelabel

marketing.campaign_target: links a campaign to what it promotes
marketing.customer_badge: badges awarded; we have challenge and challenge_progress and no badge
marketing.customer_challenge_progress: the table name repeats its schema; same habit as the 645 column renames
marketing.customer_consent: ours is marketing.consent_record and consent is not only a customer's; take their provenance fields, which trace a consent back to registration, waiver, campaign or survey
marketing.customer_segment_rule: segment_criterion is ours and customer_ repeats the schema
marketing.data_subject_request: duplicates our platform.dsar_request — flagged 18 September, still true
marketing.do_not_contact: our marketing.suppression; a suppression list is the standard word and theirs names a flag, not a list
marketing.journey_enrollment: enrollment is the clearer word; journey_entrant reads as a person, not a state
marketing.journey_step: we hold journey and journey_entrant and no steps
marketing.loyalty_campaign: links a campaign to loyalty bonuses; a different table, not a rename
marketing.loyalty_points: the points ledger; we hold loyalty_position and no transaction history
marketing.loyalty_program: our marketing.loyalty_programme. En-GB throughout the package - programme, organisation, authorisation, serialised. A convention, not a table
marketing.loyalty_rule: their earning and bonus rules; ours sit inside loyalty_programme
marketing.points_earning_rule: they split earning and redemption; our loyalty_programme holds both
marketing.points_redemption_rule: they split earning and redemption; our loyalty_programme holds both
marketing.review_response: staff replies to a review; we hold review alone
marketing.reward: we hold loyalty_programme, _tier and _position but no reward
marketing.reward_assignment: which reward went to whom; pairs with marketing.reward
marketing.sla_policy: support-case SLA, not an approvals SLA
marketing.support_case: ours already means support cases only
marketing.survey: our marketing.form_definition - it carries kind, score_scale, version and status, so NPS and CSAT are shapes of one form
marketing.survey_question: our marketing.form_definition covers surveys and waivers as one shape
marketing.waiver_signature: signature against an immutable waiver version; form_submission does not pin the version
marketing.waiver_template: our marketing.form_definition again: requires_signature, signature_kind, legal_reviewed_by, valid_for_months, minimum_age and version. The version column is why we take their waiver_signature
orders.cash_count: ours rolls cash_count_line up to the shift; theirs is the session header
orders.currency_rule: settlement currency and rounding exist nowhere in our package, and a rounding rule is venue-wide, not per method. Belongs in payments, not orders
orders.deposit: rental security deposit, not a till deposit
orders.deposit_activity: authorise, hold, capture, release, forfeit, refund. We hold stored_value_authorisation and the net figures on rental.settlement, and no history between them. A forfeited deposit is a dispute waiting to happen. Belongs in payments
orders.discount: ours is orders.order_discount, which repeats its schema. 2 change points. Note the bound on that rule: strip the prefix only where what is left still names the thing - orders.order_line does not become orders.line
orders.order: our orders.sales_order, 223 change points and 41 inbound foreign keys - the third most connected table in the package. sales_order also distinguishes it from an F&B order and a purchase order
orders.order_fee: the fee snapshot on the order. Pairs with their payment_fee_rule, which we also take: the rule lives in payments, the snapshot on the order, the same way order_discount snapshots a promotion
orders.payment_eligibility_rule: when a method is allowed for a given transaction — no gift card for a wallet top-up, no credit under 18. payments.risk_rules is fraud, not eligibility. Belongs in payments
orders.payment_fee_rule: we hold surcharge as a jsonb blob on payments.method. A blob cannot be scoped, versioned or approved — this is the table that blob wants to be. Belongs in payments, not orders
orders.payment_method_config: our payments.method already holds currencies[], channels[], venue_ids[], scope_path and min/max. Theirs normalises that into a row per method x scope; ours is the ADR-0018 config-scope pattern used by 58 other scopes. Same information, our shape
orders.pos_shift: pos_ disambiguates from workforce.shift, which they also have
orders.recommendation_activity: our promotions.recommendation_outcome, beside recommendation_experiment and _suppression. Belongs in promotions, not orders
orders.upgrade: the upgrade transaction - original line, upgraded line, amount. We serve upgrades by operation and keep no record of one, so what a guest held before an upgrade is unrecoverable
platform.cash_denomination: cash_ is meaningful but we hold no other denomination; concede if useful
platform.cell: ours is in control with 20 columns and 19 inbound FKs
platform.cell_endpoint: how one cell reaches another; we have no endpoint record
platform.device_profile: our platform.configuration_profile with scope_path, version, settings and deployed_count. Their own purpose says "a scope or workstation", and ours covers both
platform.region_setting: singular vs plural only; settle our own convention first
platform.scope: our platform.org_unit. Their name is arguably better - it matches the scope_path column 58 of our configs address - but org_unit carries 91 declared foreign keys. The same cost that decides the venue schema
platform.subscription_tier: subscription domain; ours is control.subscription_plan with cell_tier, base_price and version
platform.tier_allowance: what a tier includes. Our subscription.capacity_pack is a pack a tenant buys on top, with a price and an invoice; the included allowance is one column, control.subscription_plan.included_ai_tokens. Belongs in subscription
platform.tier_module: our subscription.module_listing.included_in_tiers[] holds it as an array on the module. Feeds the module-enablement question — we have three homes for this idea
pricing.dynamic_price_action: a pricing schema we do not have; dynamic pricing sits in catalogue and promotions for us
pricing.dynamic_price_condition: a pricing schema we do not have; dynamic pricing sits in catalogue and promotions for us
pricing.dynamic_price_rule: a pricing schema we do not have; dynamic pricing sits in catalogue and promotions for us
queue.entry: their purpose says "a customer or party"; our queue.waiting_guest misnames a party of six as a guest. 40 change points, worth it

reporting.report_schedule: the table name repeats its schema; same habit as the 645 column renames

resources.rental_agreement_item: our rental.equipment_assignment has asset_id, serial_number, assigned_at and returned_at, so partial returns already work. Take their per-item status (missing, damaged) and the quantity path for items that are not serialised
resources.rental_inspection: we give the domain its own schema; same principle they accepted for branding->whitelabel
resources.rental_inspection_item: our rental.inspection is one row per asset per phase with a single condition. Theirs is the checklist line under it — per component, structured. Belongs in rental
resources.resource_booking: the table name repeats its schema; same habit as the 645 column renames

retail.price_list: F&B/Retail stand alone; their purpose says it does not depend on Catalogue
retail.product: F&B/Retail stand alone; their purpose says it does not depend on Catalogue
retail.product_category: F&B/Retail stand alone; their purpose says it does not depend on Catalogue

seating.seat_section_row: the table name repeats its schema; same habit as the 645 column renames
